h1: Restaurant marketing in Fort Lauderdale & Broward
answer: Button Up Media is a South Florida restaurant marketing agency that helps Fort Lauderdale and Broward restaurants get found by visitors in season and keep locals coming back year-round.

card.insight: Visitors fill Las Olas in season. The restaurants that stay busy kept talking to locals all year.
card.proofLine: Broward roots: Shimuja Ramen started in Southwest Ranches

heroMedia.alt: Behind the scenes of a Button Up Media shoot with the chef at Shimuja Ramen

snapshot.h2: Fort Lauderdale runs on two speeds
paragraphsHtml: From roughly December to April, snowbirds, boaters and tourists fill Las Olas, the beach and the waterfront. Many do not know the city, so they choose with a search, a look at the map and a scan of reviews. In season, your Google listing sells more than your sign.
When season ends, the restaurants that stay busy are the ones that kept talking to Broward residents all year, in English and Spanish, instead of going quiet online until the next winter.

proof.bodyHtml: Shimuja started in Southwest Ranches, in Broward, before moving to Julia & Henry's in Downtown Miami. Its owner, Chef Kei, says many customers who come to try his ramen find it through the social media we run.

steps.h2: What we'd do first in Fort Lauderdale

items.title: Win the "near me" search before season
items.bodyHtml: Right categories, real photos, accurate hours and a steady flow of reviews, set up by early fall through our Google Business Profile service.

items.title: Sell the setting, not just the plate
items.bodyHtml: Short video of the water, the patio and the light at sunset, filmed by our crew around your service. On the water? We make dockage or parking details easy to find. See our social media service.

items.title: Keep talking to locals after season
items.bodyHtml: Content and ads aimed at Broward residents, in English and Spanish, with reasons to come in on weeknights and for happy hour.

pricingHtml: Most restaurants invest $1,500 to $5,000 a month for a coordinated program. Website builds are a one-time $1,500 or $2,000.

faqs.q: Do you work with restaurants in Fort Lauderdale and Broward?
faqs.a: Yes. We are a South Florida team and work with restaurants across the region. One of our longtime clients, Shimuja Ramen, started in Southwest Ranches.

faqs.q: How do I keep my restaurant busy after snowbird season?
faqs.a: Do not go quiet online when the visitors leave. Shift content and ads toward Broward residents, in English and Spanish, with reasons to come in on weeknights.

faqs.q: When should I start before season?
faqs.a: Ideally by early fall, ahead of the Boat Show, so your Google listing, photos and reviews are in shape and your ads are tested before the visitors arrive.

faqs.q: Do you create content in Spanish?
faqs.a: Yes. Our team is bilingual, so captions, review replies, ads and your website can run in English, Spanish or both.

cta.h2: Ready for a steadier year in Fort Lauderdale?
cta.body: Tell us about your restaurant, your season and your slow nights, and Juan will tell you what we would do first. Free, in English or Spanish.
